body.p: Status of the Application

Claims 1, 4-5, 12-13, and 17-20 are amended. Support for the amendments may be found throughout the original disclosure, for example, previously presented claims 2-3. Claims 2-3 and 10-11 are cancelled without prejudice or disclaimer. Therefore, claims 1, 4-9, 12-20 are pending.
The drawings have been accepted.

The Examiner has returned the SB/08 forms for the Information Disclosure Statements filed February 16, 2022, March 30, 2023, and August 10, 2023. All of the cited references have been considered and made of record.
Statement of Summary of Interview

Applicant thanks the Examiner for the courtesies extended during the interview of March 1, 2024. During the interview, Applicant's representative discussed proposed Amendments. No agreements were reached.
It is respectfully submitted that the instant STATEMENT OF SUBSTANCE OF
INTERVIEW complies with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. §§1.2 and 1.133 and MPEP §713.04. Claim Rejections - 35 U.S.C. § 112
Claims 3-5 and 11-13 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. 112 (pre-AIA), second paragraph, as being indefinite.
Applicant respectfully submits that claims 3 and 10 have been cancelled without
disclaimer or prejudice. Applicant further submits that claims 4-5 and 12-13 are amended for clarity and definiteness. Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of this rejection.
Claims 1-20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over PUBG Mobile
as evidenced by "[PUBG MOBILE] (noted on the IDS filed 3/30/2023 NPL 2; hereinafter
Mobile) in view of PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds as evidenced by "Molotov Cocktail"
(hereinafter "Cocktail").
Claim 1 recites:
A virtual prop control method, performed by an electronic device, the method
comprising:
displaying, in a target game application, a target virtual throw prop controlled by
a first virtual operation object;
controlling the first virtual operation object to throw the target virtual throw prop,
a target throw operation being used for throwing the target virtual throw prop;
setting a target region in the target game application as a region surrounding a
point at which the target virtual throw prop is thrown,

wherein the target region is set to reduce hit points of at least one target virtual operation object located in the target region for a first predetermined duration, and wherein the first virtual operation object and the at least one target virtual operation object respectively belong to different virtual operation object sets;
based on a second virtual operation object being set to continuously lose hit
points within a fourth predetermined duration before entering the target region,
canceling said continuous loss of the hit points of the second virtual operation object
within the fourth predetermined duration upon the second virtual operation object
entering the target region, and
reducing the hit points of the second virtual operation object at a
predetermined rate within a second predetermined duration after the second virtual
operation object enters the target region.
Applicant respectfully submits that the cited references, Mobile and Cocktail, alone or in
combination fail to disclose at least "based on a second virtual operation object being set to
continuously lose hit points within a fourth predetermined duration before entering the target
region, canceling said continuous loss of the hit points of the second virtual operation object
within the fourth predetermined duration upon the second virtual operation object entering the
target region, and reducing the hit points of the second virtual operation object at a
predetermined rate within a second predetermined duration after the second virtual operation object enters the target region," as recited in claim 1.

The Examiner cites Mobile at 1:30 as corresponding to the claimed second virtual object. However, Mobile merely displays an enemy character on "fire" for a brief period. Mobile, 1:30. At no point does Mobile disclose a second virtual object being set to continuously lose hit points for a time before entering the target region, and once the second virtual operation object enters the target region, cancelling the continuous loss from before entering the target region, and only reducing the hit points of the second virtual operation object at a predetermined rate within the second predetermined duration after entering the target region.

Cocktail does not remedy this deficiency. Cocktail merely describes that "[p]layers hit by or passing through this area will be set aflame, doing constant damage over time." Cocktail. However, at no point does Cocktail disclose a player who is hit by the weapon or is passing through this impacted area and already losing hit points for a time before entering the target region, much less disclosing that this continuous loss is stopped once the player enters the target region. Furthermore, at no point does the Cocktail reference disclose only reducing the hit points of the player at a predetermined rate within a second duration after entering the target region after stopping the loss of points from before entering the impacted area.

Therefore, Applicant respectfully submits that the cited references fail to disclose or suggest at least "based on a second virtual operation object being set to continuously lose hit points within a fourth predetermined duration before entering the target region, canceling said continuous loss of the hit points of the second virtual operation object within the fourth predetermined duration upon the second virtual operation object entering the target region, and reducing the hit points of the second virtual operation object at a predetermined rate within a
second predetermined duration after the second virtual operation object enters the target region," as recited in claim 1.
For at least the reasons stated above, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 1, and all claims dependent therefrom are patentable.
Since claims 9 and 20 recite subject matter similar to but not necessarily co-extensive
with the subject matter of claim 1, Applicant respectfully submits that claims 9 and 20 and all the claims dependent therefrom are patentable for at least the same reasons as claim 1. Conclusion

In view of the above, reconsideration and allowance of this application are now believed to be in order, and such actions are hereby solicited.
